summary:
Custody placement is the sharpest documented exposure. German prisons operate under statutory separation with a binary men and women housing model; the Criminological Research Institute of Lower Saxony reads § 170(2) of the Lower Saxony correctional act as the operating rule and reports that placement corresponding to a prisoner's gender identity has been practised only in exceptional cases. It runs a research project on the situation of transgender people in prison. Several states have amended their prison statutes in recent years to accommodate legally recognised gender diversity, and a new § 17 of the Rhineland-Palatinate prison act took effect on 1 March 2026 with no press coverage at all.

How the exception is applied in practice is unsettled, and the outcome has gone both ways. In August 2025 the chief prosecutor for Halle stated that Marla-Svenja Liebich, whose gender entry was changed to female at the end of 2024 under the Self-Determination Act, would serve an 18-month sentence for incitement at Chemnitz women's prison with placement reviewed at intake. After her extradition from Czechia she was transferred to a men's prison in July 2026 despite her legal registration as a woman since 2025; authorities cited the safety of prisoners at the women's facility, while critics characterised her gender change as an abuse of the self-determination law. A trans visitor facing pre-trial detention or sentence should not assume the registered marker determines the cell.

A Verfassungsblog essay from March 2026 argues that trans prisoners need no discriminatory special law and that ordinary anti-discrimination law should govern their placement and treatment. DW reported in August 2023 that German prisons offer few safe spaces for trans inmates, describing climate activist Penelope Frank of Last Generation, legally recorded male, who faced assignment to a men's prison if convicted. The Berlin prison administration publishes an official page in German with rules and contacts for trans, inter and non-binary persons in custody across the city's facilities; comparable published guidance for other states was not found in the sources.

Legal gender recognition is available to adults through self-determination. The Self-Determination Act took effect on 1 November 2024, having passed the Bundestag in April 2024 by 374 votes to 251, and allows a change of gender entry with three months' notice for transgender, intersex and non-binary adults. It replaced the Transsexuals Act of 1980, which had required genital surgery and sterilisation until the Federal Constitutional Court ruled those requirements unconstitutional in January 2011. An intersex 'divers' marker on birth certificates, passports and driving licences has been available since 1 January 2019 under the Third Gender Act, requiring a doctor's statement and, after clarification in April 2019, applying to intersex people rather than transgender people.

Discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation or gender identity is prohibited in health services and in education under the General Act on Equal Treatment, in force since 18 August 2006. That act is also the route used in complaints about security screening: DJ and producer BASHKKA filed a legal complaint under the Equal Treatment Act over a screening at Frankfurt Airport on 23 November 2024 in which, she alleges, officers deliberately disregarded her gender identity, an act she described as targeted, degrading transphobic harassment; she gave Resident Advisor a copy of her statement to the airport authorities. A nationwide ban on conversion therapy for minors has been in force since May 2020, with penalties of up to one year's imprisonment for practitioners and fines of €30,000 for offering, promoting or referring minors.

Access to women-only facilities is contested in practice. A Deutscher Sauna-Bund guideline from January 2025 restricting women's saunas to persons whose primary sex characteristics correspond set off public argument about registered trans women's access; trans woman Alessia Dorigo countered that claiming a trans identity on a whim is unrealistic and that identity is felt rather than declared. Tagesspiegel Queerspiegel documented how Berlin saunas and similar venues treat trans women after the Self-Determination Act took effect on 1 January 2025, following months of argument over women-protected spaces and fears that the self-declaration route would be misused.

Partner and family recognition is settled law. Same-sex couples have had legally recognised status since 2001 through registered life partnerships, which carried inheritance, alimony, health insurance, immigration, hospital and jail visitation and name-change rights; same-sex marriage with full marital and adoption rights followed on 1 October 2017, with stepchild adoption legal since 2005 and successive adoption since 2013. A Federal Court of Justice ruling in October 2018 held that the non-biological mother in a married lesbian couple is not automatically recognised on a birth certificate and must adopt; a bill to correct this was pending in the Bundestag.

Official policy has been moving in a restrictive direction on adjacent fronts. The ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 records that in June 2025 the Federal Cabinet proposed designating Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia as safe countries of origin despite LGBTI people facing imprisonment there; that in July 2025 the Education Minister banned gender-inclusive language in her ministry, which the Federal Anti-Discrimination Office said contradicts constitutional equality protection; and that in August 2025 the Merz coalition announced it would end humanitarian admission programmes, including the Afghanistan scheme for persecuted LGBTI people.

Practical support exists. The STOP the HATE campaign, run by Prevention and Empowerment in northern Germany, maintains a counselling finder sorted by topic, emergency guidance including an LSBTIQ* crisis line, and a hate-crime knowledge base covering underreporting, evidence preservation, witness support and reporting channels.
tangentialFactors:
Public hostility in this area is exercised through the media as much as through the state. In the Liebich case the press council unanimously rejected her complaint against Der Spiegel as unfounded, and a Berlin court rejected her injunction against journalist Julian Reichelt, indicating that coverage of a trans person's criminal case is difficult to suppress even where it is contested.

The legal framework has been unsettled for decades. Paragraph 175 of the German Empire's Penal Code recriminalised sex between men in 1871; Nazi enforcement produced roughly 8,000 convictions a year and 5,000 to 15,000 people interned in concentration camps. East Germany decriminalised in 1968 and West Germany in 1969, convictions from the Nazi era were overturned in 2002, and in 2017 the Bundestag unanimously passed a pardon for around 50,000 men convicted after the war, with €3,000 per conviction plus €1,500 per year of imprisonment; the compensation scheme ran from September 2021. This history shapes the legal culture in which trans protections now sit.

Health-related rules carry residual effects that a visitor may notice. Blood donation deferrals for men who have sex with men were replaced by an individual risk-based assessment from 1 April 2023, after a one-year deferral in 2017 and four months from September 2021. The German Medical Association directs members not to perform assisted reproduction for lesbian couples, a directive that is not legally binding.

Concealment remains common. According to the EU Fundamental Rights Agency's 2013 survey, two-thirds of 20,000 German LGBT respondents concealed their sexual orientation at school and in public life. In May 2019 the Federal Minister of Family Affairs recommended that teachers use gender-neutral forms such as 'parent 1 and parent 2'.
localsOnly:
Residents can change their legal gender entry through the self-declaration route introduced by the Self-Determination Act on 1 November 2024, with three months' notice to the registry office and no surgery or sterilisation requirement. Intersex, transgender and non-binary adults are all covered; the separate 'divers' marker introduced on 1 January 2019 remains tied to a doctor's statement confirming intersex status and is not available to transgender people.

Discrimination complaints in employment, health services and education go through the General Act on Equal Treatment, and the Federal Anti-Discrimination Office commented publicly in July 2025 that the Education Ministry's ban on gender-inclusive language contradicts constitutional equality protection. Conversion therapy for minors has been banned nationwide since May 2020 with penalties of up to one year in prison and fines of €30,000.

Residents in custody in Berlin have a dedicated official page from the Berlin prison administration covering rules and contacts for trans, inter and non-binary persons across the city's facilities. Prison statutes in several states have been amended to accommodate legally recognised gender diversity, and Rhineland-Palatinate's § 17 has been in force since 1 March 2026. Ordinary anti-discrimination law, rather than a trans-specific statute, is what commentators propose should govern placement and treatment.

Local support includes the STOP the HATE counselling finder, an LSBTIQ* crisis line, and a hate-crime knowledge base with guidance on evidence preservation, witness support and reporting channels. Partner recognition for same-sex couples has been available since 2001 and full marriage since 2017, including hospital and jail visitation rights inherited from the registered partnership framework.

Unresolved: the outcome of BASHKKA's Equal Treatment Act complaint about the 23 November 2024 Frankfurt Airport screening is not reported. The filing and her description of the incident are sourced; the proceeding's result is not.

Unresolved: the bill initiated by the Greens in June 2018 to correct the Federal Court of Justice's October 2018 birth-certificate ruling was pending in the Bundestag at the time of the source; its current status is not sourced here.

Unresolved: the Berlin prison service page is the only facility-level guidance located. Whether other state prison administrations publish equivalent material was not verified in this inventory, and Berlin's rules should not be assumed to apply in other states.
